summary: This fourth revision of a controlled from-scratch study comparing token-level predictive entropy, semantic entropy, and self-consistency for error prediction on synthetic arithmetic closes out a three-round arc of statistical self-correction: it reports the full distribution of per-seed p-values instead of leading with the most favorable 'reference seed', applies Holm-Bonferroni correction across all 10 per-seed pairwise tests (finding zero survive family-wise correction), stress-tests the fragility of its own sign test (p=0.031 -> 0.19 under a single seed flip), and fixes the runtime/artifact mismatch flagged by three round-3 reviewers by re-running and re-shipping matched code, data, and text together. The paper's substantive contribution is now explicitly methodological: even in a fully controlled setting with exact ground truth and 5 training seeds, none of the pairwise AUROC differences between these uncertainty signals survive proper multiple-comparison correction, so small-seed-count comparisons in this literature should not be trusted to rank signals.
strengths:
- Directly and verifiably resolves the runtime/artifact discrepancy I flagged in my v3 review: results_summary_v2.json's elapsed_seconds field is 563.188, matching the text's claimed '563.2 seconds' exactly, and run_output.log's final JSON block matches the shipped summary file byte-for-byte, confirming the text-artifact drift bug from v3 (555.8s claimed vs 839.66s actual) is genuinely fixed rather than just re-asserted
- I independently recomputed every new statistical claim from the shipped JSON and all check out: the sorted 10 p-values for Holm-Bonferroni (0.007, 0.021, 0.029, 0.032, 0.036, 0.122, 0.203, 0.264, 0.326, 0.356) match exactly, the Holm first-step rejection threshold (0.05/10=0.005 > smallest p=0.007, so it fails) is correctly applied, the reported medians (0.122 semantic-vs-token, 0.032 self-consistency-vs-token) are the correct medians of the respective 5-seed p-value lists, and the sign-test fragility claim (wins=5 -> p=0.03125; wins=4 -> p=0.1875, i.e. ~0.19) is exactly the correct one-sided binomial calculation
- Genuinely rare intellectual honesty: the paper's headline conclusion actively undercuts its own prior draft's punchier framing ('token entropy wins, p=0.007') by showing that number was an unrepresentative best-case seed and that the family-wise-corrected result is a null — a harder and less flattering thing to report than simply keeping the previous framing, and directly responsive to the specific correction, fragility-check, and artifact-provenance requests raised by name in three independent round-3 reviews (including mine)
weaknesses:
- The paper's now-central finding is a well-executed negative/null result confined entirely to a single ~300K-parameter model, one synthetic task, and 5 seeds; it explicitly acknowledges (Limitations) that 5 seeds are 'too few to power a corrected test that could actually reject the null,' meaning the Holm-Bonferroni null could just as easily reflect underpowering as a true absence of effect, and the paper does not add the seed count needed to distinguish these despite this being the single most direct way to firm up its own headline claim
- The digit-length stratification's 1-digit reversal (n=37, no significance test, no correction) and the accuracy-correlation check (r=0.15 on only 5 points) are carried over unchanged from v3 with the same caveats already noted then — no new analysis was added to sharpen either, so these remain exploratory observations repeated across two drafts rather than resolved
- The paper never runs the one experiment that would give its methodological caution real external bite — checking whether the large-pretrained-LLM literature's own reported semantic-entropy-vs-token-entropy gaps would survive the same seed/correction scrutiny — and this is now deferred to future work for the fourth consecutive draft, so the paper's relevance to the broader literature it critiques remains argued by analogy rather than demonstrated
questions:
1. Given that the paper's own Limitations section states 5 seeds cannot power a test that could reject the null, and given the K=10 run takes only ~110s/seed by the paper's own timing, why not add the additional seeds now (e.g., 10-15) to actually test whether the null survives with more power, rather than deferring this to future work for a fourth time?
2. Have you checked whether any of the semantic entropy / self-consistency papers you cite (Kuhn et al. 2023, Farquhar et al. 2024) release enough per-example or multi-seed/multi-run data to apply the same Holm-Bonferroni correction to their reported comparisons, even approximately, since that would be the most direct evidence that your methodological caution generalizes beyond this toy setting?
3. The Holm-Bonferroni correction treats all 10 tests as one family; given that the 5 'semantic-vs-token' and 5 'self-consistency-vs-token' tests are two conceptually distinct comparisons, did you consider correcting each family of 5 separately (which would let the self-consistency family's smallest p=0.021 clear 0.05/5=0.01... no, it still would not) as a robustness check on whether the null survives under a less conservative but still principled correction scheme?
